facts.claim: Tuple is a remote pair programming app for developers.
facts.excerpt: Tuple is an app for remote pair programming, optimized for everything that developers care about

facts.claim: Tuple is positioned as the best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows.
facts.excerpt:
# Tuple

### The best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows

facts.claim: Tuple emphasizes seamless collaboration with full-time mouse and keyboard support for both parties.
facts.excerpt: Seamless collaboration with full-time mouse and keyboard support for both parties

facts.claim: Tuple advertises snappy interactions, command-line integration, and pluginability.
facts.excerpt: snappy interactions, command-line integration and pluginability.

facts.claim: Tuple has a Slack integration that starts pairing sessions from channels or DMs using a /tuple command.
facts.excerpt: Tuple's integration for Slack adds a `/tuple` command, which will start a pairing session directly from a channel or DMs.

facts.claim: Tuple offers a free-forever account for educational purposes on request.
facts.excerpt: if you email support@tuple.app and say you want to use Tuple for educational purposes, we'll make you a free-forever account.
facts.source_title: Tuple: Pair Programming Tool for macOS | Hacker News

facts.claim: Tuple says it is optimized for developers who care about high-fidelity remote control and mouse cursors for all participants.
facts.excerpt: a world where you want mouse cursors for all participants and high-fidelity remote control (like Command+Tab support).

research.website_note: The results tie tuple.app to Tuple through its official site, LinkedIn page, and GitHub organization.

strategy.observation: Tuple’s Slack integration lets teams start pair programming sessions from channels or DMs with a /tuple command, which points to a team-workflow use case rather than just an individual-dev tool.
strategy.offer_link: Video case studies featuring engineering teams would give Tuple a concrete way to show that team-workflow in action, especially how real teams adopt Tuple from Slack and use it inside day-to-day engineering collaboration.
hypotheses: Tuple’s marketing team may be looking for more proof-driven content to support demand generation.
Engineering-team customer stories may be especially persuasive for developers evaluating collaboration tools.
Tuple may want more bottom-of-funnel assets that show real workflows rather than feature descriptions.
strategy.angle: Tuple’s Slack pairing workflow makes it a natural fit for short customer videos showing engineering teams starting sessions from the tools they already use.
strategy.fit_reason: Tuple is a plausible fit because it sells a developer collaboration tool that can benefit from customer proof, but the facts do not show a stated need for case studies or a current campaign where video stories are clearly required.

draft.subject: Slack workflow stories
draft.body:
Tuple’s /tuple flow stands out. Starting a pairing session from Slack or a DM makes the workflow feel team-level, not just individual-dev.

I make short video case studies with engineering teams. My guess is those stories would show the handoff from Slack to live pairing in a way feature pages can’t.
